explanation:
**What the grids are made of.** Every input has two full-length lines of distinct colours on opposite edges (top/bottom in pairs 1 and 3, left/right in pair 2), a black background, and scattered single green (3) dots. In the output the lines are unchanged and the colour 3 disappears: every dot has been recoloured to one of the two line colours.

**Which colour each dot gets.** Comparing changed cells against the line positions: in pair 1 the dots at rows 2–3 became 4 (the top line's colour, row 0) and the dots at rows 6–7 became 7 (the bottom line, row 9). In pair 2, with vertical lines at x=0 (colour 1) and x=9 (colour 2), the dot at x=6 became 2 and the dots at x=4 and x=2 became 1. Pair 3 behaves the same way with 8/9. So each dot takes the colour of the **nearest line**, measured perpendicular to the lines. There are no ties in any pair (lines at index 0 and 9 give distances 4 vs 5 for the middle columns).

**Applying it to the test input.** The lines are vertical: colour 5 at x=0 and colour 4 at x=9. Dots at x=1,2,3,4 (distance to the left line ≤4, to the right ≥5) become 5; dots at x=5,6,8 become 4. The construction in the program does this in two stages: first recolour all dots closest to the first line, then all dots closest to the second line.
